simple_answer: Employees are entitled to multiple types of leave including Casual Leave, Sick Leave, Earned Leave, Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Bereavement Leave, and Loss of Pay. Casual Leave is 12 days per year, Sick Leave is 10 days per year, and Earned Leave is 15 days per year. Leave approval depends on leave balance, manager approval, project workload, and business continuity requirements. Emergency leave must be informed within 24 hours. Leave during notice period may be restricted and excessive leave without approval may affect appraisal and promotion eligibility.
red_flags: Leave without prior approval may be treated as absenteeism
Frequent unplanned leave may negatively affect appraisal and promotion
Insufficient leave balance may result in Loss of Pay salary deduction
Long leave during notice period may be rejected or adjusted against notice buyout
Repeated sick leave without valid medical proof may trigger HR review
Ignoring manager approval may lead to formal warning
Leave misuse during critical project deadlines may impact manager trust
practical_advice: Always check your leave balance before applying for leave
Apply leave through HRMS portal or official leave request email
For emergency leave, inform your reporting manager and HR within 24 hours
Plan long leave requests at least 7 working days in advance
Keep medical certificates ready for sick leave exceeding 2 days
Discuss notice period leave plans before resignation
Ensure proper work handover before extended leave approval
negotiation_tips: Discuss planned leave early with your manager instead of last-minute requests
Clarify leave approval conditions during notice period before resigning
Request leave adjustments instead of immediate rejection if project deadlines exist
Ask HR whether Earned Leave can be encashed during final settlement
Confirm sandwich leave rules for weekends and public holidays

simple_answer: Promotion is based on minimum tenure, performance consistency, appraisal ratings, attendance discipline, leadership readiness, manager recommendation, and business requirements. Employees usually need at least 12 months in their current role and strong performance ratings to be considered. Employees on probation, notice period, or active disciplinary review are generally not eligible. Promotions are reviewed twice a year during formal promotion cycles and require reporting manager, HR, department head, and final leadership approval.
red_flags: Promotion is not guaranteed based only on years of service
Poor attendance may delay or block promotion eligibility
Disciplinary actions or warning notices can prevent promotion approval
Employees on probation or notice period are generally not eligible
No available higher role may delay promotion despite strong performance
Manager recommendation alone does not guarantee promotion approval
Promotion discussions without written approval are not final
practical_advice: Build leadership and ownership beyond daily assigned work
Avoid attendance issues and policy violations
Discuss career growth regularly with your reporting manager
Track promotion review cycles during April and October
negotiation_tips: Request formal feedback before promotion discussions
Ask for promotion review during appraisal cycles instead of random requests
Clarify required skill gaps for the next role
Discuss salary revision separately from designation change
Understand business availability before expecting immediate promotion
